scenario: A payroll utility must parse employee hours and rates without accepting invalid or missing values.
lab: Implement a command-line payroll calculator with an Employee value object. Parse employee ID, hours and rate; calculate gross pay; reject blank IDs, negative hours and negative rates.
output: Java source, test cases and a sample payroll report
outcomes: Calculate gross pay for valid decimal inputs
Separate parsing errors from business-rule errors
checks: Employee E01, 40 hours and rate 25.50 produces gross pay 1020.00
A blank ID or negative hours is rejected without producing a payroll row
Three valid employees retain their original IDs and report total gross pay equal to the sum of individual pays

scenario: A support queue must route tickets by priority and reject unknown severities.
lab: Create a pure routeTicket method that maps P1, P2 and P3 tickets to response targets. Process a supplied list, count each priority and reject an unknown P4 value with a descriptive exception.
output: Ticket-routing class, unit tests and priority summary
outcomes: Use conditional logic without duplicating routing rules
Test normal and invalid ticket priorities
checks: P1 maps to the documented urgent target and P3 to the standard target
A P4 ticket is rejected and does not affect the summary count
A five-ticket fixture produces the expected P1, P2 and P3 counts

topic: DevOps Orientation, SDLC and Agile Delivery
scenario: A team has a production defect but no shared definition of done or release evidence.
lab: Map a supplied feature from backlog item through code review, automated checks, staging deployment and release decision. Define acceptance criteria, owner, evidence and rollback trigger for each stage.
output: Delivery workflow board, definition of done and release-evidence checklist
outcomes: Distinguish deployment activity from evidence that a change is releasable
Identify missing approval and rollback information
checks: Every workflow stage has an owner, input and evidence output
A failed automated check prevents the release decision from being marked ready
The rollback trigger names a measurable operational condition rather than a vague concern

scenario: A service is using disk space rapidly and its owner needs evidence before cleanup.
lab: Use a disposable Linux training environment to inspect files, permissions, processes and disk use. Locate a supplied oversized log, compare its owner and permissions, and create a safe archival plan without deleting it.
output: Command transcript, disk-use report and reviewed archival plan
outcomes: Interpret file ownership, permissions and disk usage
Collect evidence before proposing a change
checks: The report identifies the seeded oversized file and its size
The participant explains why its permission bits allow or deny the named user action
The plan avoids deleting live files and states the verification step after archival
prerequisites: Shell access and basic file concepts

scenario: A sales manager needs a report whose totals can be traced to the source rows.
lab: Load a supplied ten-row sales table into Power BI, create revenue and order-count measures, then build a page with a monthly trend and regional breakdown. Reconcile visuals to a supporting table.
output: Power BI report, measure definitions and reconciliation note
outcomes: Create explicit measures rather than relying on implicit aggregation
Explain how report filters affect a visual
checks: The revenue card equals the sum of the ten supplied sales rows
A region filter changes both the trend and supporting table consistently
Order count remains distinct from revenue and both visuals have labeled units
prerequisites: Spreadsheet tables and basic business metrics

scenario: A dashboard shows a missing month as zero and leads stakeholders to infer a sales collapse.
lab: Extend the supplied report with a date table and monthly visual. Preserve the missing month as missing data, add a report-level date filter and document the selected missing-data treatment.
output: Updated report page and missing-data decision note
outcomes: Distinguish a missing observation from a zero-value observation
Validate filter context using a supporting table
checks: The missing month is not silently displayed as zero revenue
Changing the date filter updates all specified visuals consistently
The note explains the data-quality limitation and identifies the source owner to contact
prerequisites: Power BI report creation and basic date fields

scenario: A team proposes an autonomous agent for a task that may only need a deterministic workflow.
lab: Classify six supplied business cases as rules-based automation, generative AI, retrieval-assisted generation, or agentic workflow. For each, identify input data, allowed actions, human approval point and a reason not to use a more autonomous approach.
output: Six-case decision matrix and architecture sketch for one selected case
outcomes: Choose an approach based on task uncertainty and action risk
Identify when human approval is required
checks: Each case has one selected approach and evidence-based rationale
High-impact actions include an explicit approval or deny path
The proposed agent case names tools, boundaries and a failure escalation rather than claiming autonomy is always better
prerequisites: Basic software systems and business-process concepts

scenario: An assistant gives different answers to the same support request and invents a customer field.
lab: Run a supplied prompt against a controlled sample context using two temperature settings. Compare outputs, identify unsupported fields, then constrain the required JSON response to known schema fields and an unknowns list.
output: Prompt variants, output comparison and constrained response schema
outcomes: Explain how context, sampling and schema constraints affect an agent response
Detect unsupported claims against supplied source context
checks: The constrained output contains only allowed field names
Unknown information is returned as an explicit unknown rather than an invented value
The comparison records response variation without claiming a single setting guarantees correctness
prerequisites: JSON, APIs and basic prompt concepts

scenario: A registration page is unusable with a keyboard and submits incomplete profile data.
lab: Build a semantic registration form with associated labels, required fields, error messages and a confirmation region. Test it using keyboard-only navigation and submitted invalid and valid sample values.
output: HTML page, accessibility checklist and form test evidence
outcomes: Use semantic form controls and associated labels
Describe client-side validation limits
checks: Every input has an associated visible label
Tab order reaches all interactive controls in the expected sequence
Invalid email is reported clearly and valid input reaches the confirmation region without claiming server-side validation

scenario: A product card layout overflows on a narrow viewport and hides the action button.
lab: Style a supplied product-card page using responsive layout rules. Test at 320px, 768px and 1440px widths; preserve readable text, visible controls and the declared card order.
output: CSS stylesheet, three viewport screenshots and layout decision note
outcomes: Use responsive layout rules instead of device-specific hard-coded positions
Verify a layout at defined viewport widths
checks: At 320px no horizontal overflow hides card content or the action button
At 768px and 1440px cards follow the documented layout rule
Text, focus indication and controls remain visible at all three widths
prerequisites: HTML elements, CSS selectors and browser developer tools
